    Orcs¶

    A civilized, rational species on Ge'or. Orcs are not inherently evil, though they possess natural tendencies toward aggression and physical strength that other races view with suspicion. This double standard persists despite orcish societies like Augamouth proving their capacity for governance, culture, and diplomacy.

    Biology¶

    • Appearance: Orcs are tall and powerfully built, standing 6'0" to 6'8" (males) and 5'8" to 6'2" (females). Skin tones range from deep green to gray-green, with occasional brown variants. Prominent lower canines (tusks) are present in both sexes, though males' are typically larger. Musculature is dense — an average orc is roughly 40% stronger than an average human of equivalent size.
    • Lifespan: 55–75 years. Orcs mature faster than humans (adulthood at 14) and remain physically vigorous until their final years. Old age hits rapidly — an orc who is fighting-fit at 70 may be dead within two years.
    • Mage-cell expression: Low to moderate. Orcish magic tends toward enhancement — temporary strength boosts, battle fury, pain suppression. Elemental magic is rare. Orcish mages (called Blood-Speakers) are valued but uncommon — roughly one in two hundred.
    • Adaptation: Dense bone structure, high pain tolerance, accelerated healing of muscle and skin wounds. Orcs can fight through injuries that would incapacitate other species. This is not supernatural — it is biology refined by millennia of selection pressure on the harsh Demon Continent.

    Subraces¶

    • Yak — smaller frame (5'4"–5'10"), gray-brown skin, more modest temperament. Isolation on Yak Island selected for cooperation over competition. Nation: Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent).
    • Mountain Orcs — the original stock from which other subspecies diverged. Larger, greener, more aggressive. Found in the highlands of the Demon Continent. Not a formal nation — mountain orc clans are nomadic, following herd migrations.
    • Lowland Orcs — the most common subspecies. Brown-green skin, adapted to temperate climates. Form the population base of nations like Augamouth and Oda.

    Society¶

    Orcish society is organized around clans — extended family units of 50 to 500 individuals who share a common ancestor, territory, and honor-code. Clans are the fundamental unit of orcish life, more important than nation or species identity.

    • Nations: Augamouth (West Erisdar), Oda (Kutten), Yakut (Yak Island, Demon Continent)
    • Governance: Clan-based with a king or chieftain selected by combat and council. In Augamouth, the king rules with the Council of Elders — one representative per major clan. The king can be challenged for leadership at any Gathering (annual assembly). A weak king is expected to fall. A strong king rules until death or voluntary abdication.
    • Social structure: Warriors → Elders → Craftsmen → Hunters → Youth. Shamans (Blood-Speakers) exist outside the hierarchy — they answer only to the spirits and the king.
    • Gender roles: Egalitarian by necessity. Female orcs are only slightly less strong than males and fight alongside them. Inheritance passes through the maternal line in most clans (you always know who the mother is; fathers can be uncertain in a culture with high combat mortality).

    Culture¶

    Orcish culture values four virtues above all: strength, honor, loyalty, and truth. An orc who is weak but honorable is respected. An orc who is strong but lies is cast out.

    • The Telling: An orc who wishes to make a serious accusation or confession may invoke The Telling — a ritual where they speak uninterrupted before the clan. No one may interrupt The Telling. No one may punish the speaker for what is said during it. The Telling is sacred. Even a king cannot interrupt it.
    • Scar-Remembering: Orcs do not keep written histories. They keep scars. After a significant battle, treaty, or death, attending orcs receive ritual scarification — geometric patterns cut into the shoulders or back. An old orc's body is a library. To read an orc's scars is to read their life.
    • Death-singing: When an orc dies in battle, their clan sings them into the afterlife. The song recounts every battle they fought, every enemy they killed, every oath they kept. A death-song can last hours for a great warrior. Children learn the death-songs of their ancestors before they learn to read.
    • Relations: Orcs trade freely with other species and maintain diplomatic relations. Augamouth is a recognized kingdom in West Erisdarian politics. However, orcs are still subject to the "brute" stereotype — other species assume orcs are unintelligent, violent, or "barely civilized." This prejudice is a constant source of tension.

    Religion¶

    • Ogoron — "the titanic orc" in demonic orchish. The faith of Augamouth and much of orc-kind: a supposed huge orc will avenge all the orc race for their injustices and bring peace to the world, after which all species will live in harmony. Ogoron is inside all of their hearts.

    Nations¶

    • Augamouth — orc kingdom (West Erisdar). The most diplomatically engaged orc nation. Augamouth maintains trade routes with Venner, Anos, and the Grimmel Republic. Its king, King Gorvak II (no relation to the Age 9 warlord), has pursued a policy of "strength through trade" for 30 years.
    • Oda — orc kingdom (Kutten). Smaller and more militant than Augamouth. Oda orcs believe the soft life of trade weakens the blood. They raid the Kutten desert tribes and maintain a standing army disproportionate to their population.
    • Yakut — Yak orc nation (Yak Island, Demon Continent). The Yak orcs are culturally distinct — more cooperative, less aggressive. Their isolation on Yak Island has made them the "least orcish" orcs in the eyes of mainlanders, a label they wear with pride.

    Connections¶

    • Kingdoms: Augamouth (West Erisdar), Oda (Kutten)
    • Subrace nation: Yakut (Yak Island)
    • Relations: Tension with Goblins and Gnolls (historic raiding), trade with human nations, mutual respect with Demons (shared Demon Continent heritage)
    • Ages: Present in all ages since Age 2, major role in Demonic War (Age 8)
    • Characters: King Gorvak II (Augamouth), Chief Thokkar (Oda)
